learning_outcomes.text: Articulate the construction of a numerical model with the constraints and results from experimentation.
Develop a critical perspective on the limits and complementarities of available tools.
Optimize the correlation between experimental data and numerical simulations, an essential competence to meet industrial requirements in terms of safety and innovation.
Observe the entire experimental protocol during a vertical drop crushing test on simple structures.
Exchange freely with qualified personnel to deepen understanding of technical choices and implementation constraints.
Develop the corresponding numerical model from collected data.
Critically analyze results by identifying the limits and challenges specific to each stage (experimentation, modeling, data correlation).
Mobilize acquired skills in a professional context by studying a real industrial problem.

syllabus_topics: Nature, type and classification of impacts
Constitutive laws, different resolution methods, consideration of nonlinearities...
Description, different types of tests (frontal, lateral impacts)...
Study of an analytical model for circular or square section tubes
Realization of an experimental crash test of a simple structure, numerical simulation of the test and experimental/numerical confrontations
bibliography: N. Jones, Structural Crashworthiness, Cambridge University Press, 1997
Jorge A.C. Ambrósio, Manuel F.O. Seabra Pereira, F. Pina da Silva, Crashworthiness of Transportation Systems: Structural Impact and Occupant, Springer Netherlands, 1997
degree: Diplôme d'ingénieur Centrale Nantes, spécialité Mécanique (apprentissage)
